_about: RATIFIED Company Standard — approved THROUGH THE LEGAL CONSTITUTION L1.10 (owner ruling 2026-09-13,
extended to the Section 31 document types 2026-09-18, resolving C-23). Drafted from §31.5's own words;
every value is the section's, none is invented (rule 7/21). Catalogue: docs/00-project/CLAUSE_CATALOGUE.md.
description: The Company will not solicit a Partner's introduced End Customer away in a way that circumvents the Partner's commissions.

approval.ruling: owner, 2026-09-13 as extended 2026-09-18 (C-23) — this standard restates §31.5 without changing its meaning
approval.calibration: 35.10 — NOT yet calibrated against counterparty paper; §31.5's evidence is two historical Partner Agreements not held in this repository. Re-calibrate when one is supplied (rule 21).

source_document: Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.10 — docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.10.md
source_quote: The Company will not directly solicit an End Customer introduced by a Partner to move to a different partner or a direct relationship with the Company, in a manner that would circumvent the Partner's rightful commissions or relationship, during the term of the Partner Agreement. This does not prevent general, non-targeted marketing, or accepting unsolicited orders from a customer the Partner introduced, since Partner Agreements are non-exclusive.

evaluation_rules._note: presence is established by the mapping layer alone (45D)

_calibration: Appendix B has NO clause category for non-circumvention, so `constitution.topic` takes §31.5's own heading rather than being force-fitted to an unrelated Appendix B row. That is a routing label, not a legal position; if Appendix B later gains a category, this value should move to it.
Negative patterns keep employee non-solicitation (a different clause, and one §31.5 does not address) out of this standard's mapping — the subject here is the END CUSTOMER relationship, not staff.

§31.5's second sentence is a CARVE-OUT, not a separate position: general non-targeted marketing and unsolicited orders are expressly permitted, so a Partner Agreement permitting them is not thereby a deviation.
